title: Before It Breaks audit configuration
description: One audit.config.json per audit workspace. You write it by hand (or let `kit init` start it); generated state such as pins and run logs lives in work/, never here. Fields you leave out are filled from config/defaults.json, then from the preset you name. This schema uses only a small JSON Schema subset so the kit can check it without dependencies: type, required, properties, additionalProperties, enum, const, items, minItems, pattern, minimum, default, $ref/$defs.

$schema.description: Relative path or URL of this schema, so editors can autocomplete and flag typos.

preset.description: Starting point chosen from the decision guide. Its values sit between the kit defaults and your own fields: anything you write here still wins.

size.description: Rough audit size from the decision guide (see config/sizes.json). It is guidance for planning repos, hunt groups and verify runs; it does not change any other field.

audit.description: What this audit is about, in plain words. These sentences are copied into agent prompts and report headers.

name.description: Short title used in report headings, e.g. "Notes platform growth audit".

question.description: The one question the audit must answer, e.g. "Can a single workspace hold half a million notes, and what gives way first?".

type.description: Kind of audit; normally the same as the preset.

date.description: Audit date as YYYY-MM-DD. Workflows cannot read the clock, so the date travels in through their arguments.

kit.description: Where the kit itself lives. Written by `kit init` inside a workspace; leave it out elsewhere and the kit uses its own folder.

root.description: Absolute path of the kit checkout or plugin folder.

repos.description: Every repository the audit reads. Code is only ever read; nothing in these folders is changed.

scale.description: The size that matters and the size you are aiming for. Thresholds are reported against these tiers.

unit.description: The growing quantity, said in full, e.g. "notes in one workspace".

unit_short.description: One-word form used in tables, e.g. "notes". Defaults to the last word of `unit`.

target.description: The size you want one tenant (or the unit's owner) to reach.

platform_target.description: Optional size for the whole platform (all tenants together). Must be at least `target`.

tiers.description: Strictly ascending sizes at which findings are graded. Every tier must be at most `target`. Left out: 10000 and 100000 (those below the target) followed by the target itself.

bases.description: Allowed answers to "what does this finding grow with?". The defaults cover per-tenant data, platform data, fan-out, file rows, and items that do not depend on size.

known_limits.description: Hard limits of the platform that agents may rely on without proving them again, e.g. "Edge proxy rejects request bodies over 2 MiB".

library_assumptions.description: Library behaviours the hunters and skeptics should check, each one line, e.g. "queue library: a failed job id cannot be reused until removed".

out_of_scope.description: Topics agents must not report on; anything they notice there goes to notes, not findings. Example: "security", "legacy import tool".

lenses.description: Hunt lenses in use. Each one is a method file the hunters read first (method/lenses/<lens>.md). The kit ships performance, reliability, data, infra and frontend; any other name must also appear in custom_lenses.

custom_lenses.description: Lenses you wrote yourself, e.g. "search-index". Listing one here lets `lenses` use it; you must also provide its lens file.

groups.description: Hunt groups: one hunter agent per group, each with one repo and one lens.

areas.description: Report sections that findings are filed under, e.g. "background jobs", "database and indexes".

modules.description: How file paths map to named modules in the architecture view. The first rule whose pattern matches a path wins.

severity_rubric.description: Severity levels and what each means, in report order (most severe first).

effort_scale.description: Effort sizes for recommended fixes and what each means, smallest first.

verify.description: How candidate findings are challenged before they count.

skeptic_lenses.description: One skeptic per lens tries to refute each candidate. At least three, so a cut in budget never cuts the checks.

survive_votes.description: How many skeptics must fail to refute a candidate for it to survive. At most the number of skeptic lenses.

models.description: Model and effort per role. Leave a role out to keep its default; `inherit` means the workflow sends no model option and the session's model is used.

agents.description: How agent types are named. With the plugin installed the namespace is the plugin name plus a colon; after `kit install-agents` set it to an empty string.

namespace.description: Prefix put in front of every agent type.

types.description: Agent file name per role (without the namespace).

concurrency.description: Limits on how many agents run. Larger phases are split into several workflow runs.

max_agents_per_workflow.description: Most agents one workflow run may start.

max_concurrent.description: Most agents running at the same moment. At most `max_agents_per_workflow`.

verify_pool.description: Verify batches worked on in parallel.

evidence.description: Rules for re-running the read-only commands that back each finding.

shell.description: `auto` finds a POSIX shell (Git Bash on Windows); otherwise give `bash` or an absolute path to one.

timeout_ms.description: Time limit per command, in milliseconds.

allowed_heads.description: Programs a command may start with. Anything else is skipped as unsafe.

live_prefixes.description: Command starts that need a live system (a database shell, say). Those commands are recorded but not run by the kit.

secret_patterns.description: JavaScript regular expressions (case-insensitive) whose matches are masked in captured output. Your entries are added to the kit's default masks; the defaults cannot be removed.

rules.description: Static-analysis rules run over the repos.

enabled.description: Turn the rules stage off for stacks the bundled rules do not cover.

engine.description: Rule engine. Only Semgrep is supported.

sets.description: Bundled rule folders under rules/semgrep/ to use.

outputs.description: File and folder names of the deliverables, relative to the workspace; target_architecture is a file name inside docs_dir.

publish.description: Where results are published, which decides link formats and the issue export.

tracker.description: Issue tracker: `gitlab` writes a CSV import, `github` a markdown checklist, `none` nothing.

base_url.description: Web address of the repository that will hold the docs, used to build links. Empty keeps links relative.

docs_host.description: Which host's markdown and diagram rendering the docs should suit.

measure.description: The measure phase (designed, not yet proven): what access unlocks which checks, and how commands are sorted by kind.

access.description: Access levels you may grant, the safe way to grant each, and what each one makes provable.

kinds.description: Measurement kind -> JavaScript regular expression matched against a command.

read_only.description: Commands the audit session must never run. `kit init` turns them into deny rules in the workspace's .claude/settings.json.

deny_bash.description: Command prefixes to deny. Your entries are added to the kit's default list; the defaults cannot be removed.

repo.description: One repository. Give `path` normally; in an example plan you may give `url` and `ref` (and a `pin`, which may be "TODO") instead.

name.description: Short kebab-case name used everywhere else, e.g. "notes-api".

path.description: Folder of the checkout, absolute or relative to the workspace.

ref.description: Tag or branch to clone (example plans).

pin.description: Commit the example plan was written against, or "TODO" until it is chosen.

role.description: What the repo is, which picks the mapper checklist.

include.description: Folders or files to read, relative to the repo. Empty means the whole repo.

exclude.description: Folders or files to skip, relative to the repo.

context_only.description: Read for context (e.g. deployment manifests) but never hunted in; no group may point at it.

known_gaps.description: Things you know the audit cannot see in this repo, stated in the report's limits.

key.description: Upper-case id such as "SVC-JOBS"; it prefixes every candidate the group finds.

repo.description: Name of a repo from `repos` that is not context-only.

scope.description: Which code this hunter reads, e.g. "src/jobs/ and the queue setup".

focus.description: What to look for first, in a sentence.

claims.description: Ids of earlier-audit claims (work/claims.json) this group must re-check.

maps.description: Phase-1 map files the hunter reads before starting.

pattern.description: JavaScript regular expression matched against repo-relative paths; capture groups can be used as $1, $2 in `id` and `label`.

doc.description: Workspace-relative link to the module's description.

modelChoice.description: Model and effort for one role.

model.description: `opus`, `sonnet`, `fable`, `inherit`, or a full model id starting with "claude-".
